TRAINING The Contractor shall provide a comprehensive onsite training program for the operating clinicians. This training program shall include at the minimum the following sessions: (i) Technical Training, (ii) Operational Training, (iii) Administrative Training, and (iv) Hardware and Software Troubleshooting. Training shall occur onsite during normal business hours, 7:00am-3:30pm, Monday through Friday. Competency assessments shall be provided with the training. Onsite training is to be scheduled in advance with the Providence VA Medical Center through the COR. The Contractor shall provide onsite general overview technical training for Clinical Engineering personnel as requested. Training shall include a technical overview of the mechanics, electronics, and general operations of the system. Training shall cover detailed instruction regarding the preventative maintenance, troubleshooting, and general maintenance of the equipment. 5. INSPECTION AND ACCEPTANCE The Contractor shall conduct a joint inspection with the COR upon delivery of equipment. Contractor shall provide dates of completion of punch list items and replacement parts and/or short ship items from the manufacturer(s). The COR shall ensure all work is completed satisfactorily prior to acceptance. Disputes shall be resolved by the Contracting Officer. 6. WARRANTY The contractor shall provide a one year manufacturer’s warranty on all parts and labor. The warranty shall include all travel and shipping costs associated with any warranty repair. 7. INDONESIA

Indonesia Disaster Risk Finance & Insurance

Disaster Risk Management and Financing

GENERAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE

Grant No. TF0B4675

Project ID No. P173249

 

The Government of Indonesia  has received financing in the amount of US$ 10,000,000 equivalent from the World Bank toward the cost of the Indonesia Disaster Risk Finance & Insurance, and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services to be procured under this project.

 

The project will include the following:

Component 1: Establishing and capitalizing the P

o strengthen PFB operations.

 

Component 2: Improving Preparedness for More Effective Disaster Response Across Government Agencies.

This component will support MOF to build the disbursement channels for resources from the PFB to flow efficiently, effectively, and transparently. This will be achieved through actions that streamline processes and set up programs to quickly allocate and disburse funds to relevant ministries and agencies to be used through existing government systems for enhanced preparedness, response, and rehabilitation. Specifically, this will include the following activities: (i) Budget tracking to strengthen disaster related fiscal effectiveness; (ii) Supporting disaster preparedness and early action; (iii) Supporting subnational governments in disaster preparedness and response; (iv) Supporting faster social assistance payments for disaster victims through Adaptive Social Protection; (v) Supporting improved health preparedness and response to disasters.

 

Component 3: Strengthening PFB capacity and systems to effectively support risk finance and disaster response.

This component will support MoF to achieve the PBCs and associated results under Component 1 and Component 2.

esting, and Preventive Maintenance 1. Project Title GWMP Emergency Generator 2. Agency / Location George Washington Memorial Parkway (GWMP) 3. Objective A; The purpose of this Statement of Work (SOW) is to establish a Base Period plus Four (4) Option Periods contract for the REPLACEMENT of three (3) as like generators for operational readiness of GWMP-owned emergency generators. The Contractor shall replace as like and shall perform inspections, testing, adjustments, and preventive maintenance services to ensure generators remain in a reliable state of readiness to provide uninterrupted emergency power. OR B; The objective of this Statement of Work (SOW) is to establish a Base Period plus Four (4) Option Periods contract for the REPAIR, inspection, preventive maintenance, testing, and operational readiness of existing GWMP-owned emergency generators. The Contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, materials, tools, equipment, and incidental services necessary to ensure all generators remain fully operational and capable of providing uninterrupted emergency power in accordance with manufacturer recommendations, applicable codes, and industry standards. Services shall include routine inspections, testing, adjustments, troubleshooting, preventive maintenance, emergency/after

fter hour repairs, consumable parts and ﬂuids. corrective repairs, replacement of defective or worn components, ongoing operational monitoring, and bi-annual load bank testing to verify system reliability and performance. Non-consumable items, including major parts, components, and equipment requiring repair or replacement outside the scope of routine maintenance, shall be separately priced on an as-needed basis through a Request for Quote (RFQ) issued by the Contracting Officer (CO). Labor costs associated with such repair or replacement services shall be determined in accordance with the pricing established under the contract. 4. Scope of Work The Contractor is responsible to repair/Replace 3 each Generators to serviceable/working conditions to include furnishing all labor, supervision, tools, materials, equipment, transportation, and incidentals necessary to perform preventive maintenance and inspection services on GWMP emergency generator systems. Services shall be performed on a total of 4 generators in accordance with manufacturer guidelines, industry best practices, and applicable codes and regulations. Preventive Maintenance services shall include, but are not limited to, the inspection, testing, adjustment, and servicing of the following generator system components:

separators. • Inspect the entire fuel system for leaks. • Inspect electronic governor connections and actuator operation. • Inspect steel fuel lines for leaks, cracks, and proper support. 4.4 Fuel System – Gaseous (Natural Gas / Propane) • Inspect fuel system for gas leaks. • Inspect ignition system components, including spark plug wires and ignition coils. • Inspect and adjust governor and actuator linkage as required. 4.5 Starting System • Record battery electrolyte speciﬁc gravity for accessible batteries. • Top off electrolyte in lead-acid batteries using distilled water. • Verify and record battery charger and alternator output. • Verify proper cranking termination during startup. • Clean battery terminals and apply corrosion inhibitor as required. • Inspect and tighten battery cable and starter motor connections. 4.6 Exhaust System • Inspect ﬂexible exhaust couplings for cracks, leaks, or missing hardware. • Inspect exhaust manifolds for oil or fuel residue. • Inspect exhaust rain caps and outlet screening. • Drain exhaust moisture traps as required. 4.7 Air Intake System • Inspect air ﬁlters for restriction or deterioration; clean or replace as required (if included). • Inspect intake piping for damage or loose connections. • Inspect air cleaner
